_doc: M7-05 — the strings the Board screen (S05) shows, and nothing else. It exists because X-04 requires every user-facing string to be a loc key in EN and DE from day one, and because ContentInvariants.CheckLocaleKeyReferences fails a loc key that nothing in the content set names — a key referenced only from C# is an orphan, and an orphan is fatal. This document is that naming. The `block` group is the load-bearing one: a roll can be refused for four different reasons that all arrive on the wire as the single value ILLEGAL_STATE, so the screen names the cause from the run's own state and needs one sentence per cause. Two of those sentences are one unresolved tile told apart by WHICH tile it is: block.tile is the ordinary case, and block.gate is the mini-boss node a move may not carry past — a player who has just had a roll shortened by that rule is told nothing by 'resolve this tile', and this is the only moment on the screen where the shortened move can be explained where it happened. label.gate is its counterpart and the more important of the two, because it is read BEFORE the rule costs anything: a barred node is drawn as a shape, and a shape on a screen with no icon set, no legend and no tooltip is a rule the player can see and cannot read, so the shape says which node and this string says what it does. It also covers the one thing no mark can — nothing skips the fight, an armed escape included. The `tile` group carries all fifteen tile names because the run's pending tile arrives as a bare integer and the screen has to say what the player is standing on. The `forkLabel` group is new with the real board: BoardView.Project hands the client the bias label each branch's tiles were actually drawn under, so the two branch buttons name where they go instead of naming their structural position. The `dice` group is the fixed dice (`04` §6): a tray heading over the numbers the run holds, and the prompt that asks the player to name a number for one it has been granted. Neither carries a numeral — a die's number is drawn as a numeral on its own control, which needs no translation. Deliberately absent, each because a later milestone owns it: the perks list, the consumable pouch, and every battle, draft, shop, event and campfire caption. The `action.skipUnbuilt` and `block.unbuiltScreen` pair is the one thing here that is not a finished screen's string: an Event tile and a Minigame tile are each left by a command only their own screen submits, neither screen is built, and RESOLVE_TILE clears neither — so a run that landed on one was parked with the roll refused and ABANDON_RUN as its only exit. The board resolves them through their own commands instead, and these two strings are what it says while doing so: the control admits it is skipping rather than continuing, and the sentence names the missing screen. Both go when the screens land. The three `overview` captions are the board becoming a place the camera rides through (`16` D67): they name one control's three states — the stage, the whole board, the hero — and that control is the compliance mechanism for D42's visibility rule as D67 amended it, so the player must be able to read what pressing it will do. Three rather than two because a whole-board framing on a long chapter draws every tile below `03` §8's mandatory 48 dp, and a promise of visibility kept only on the shortest board is not kept. Gone rather than absent: the reroll's caption, its 'changes the next roll' sentence, its exhausted-refusal line and the die panel's control, all removed with the reroll and the die's special faces.
